title: Token-banking admission + prioritized shedding for cross-region dependency pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a token-banking admission controller that grants per-tenant, per-priority tokens to downstream connection pools across regions. This mechanism aims to: (1) maintain user-facing P99 latency SLOs by preventing flood-of-connections to degraded stores, (2) allow prioritized tenants/paths to continue serving while low-priority traffic is shed, and (3) support seamless multi-region failover with predictable degradation profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Mechanism issues threaded tokens to connection pools such that total active tokens per region are bounded and configurable per-store (Redis/Kafka/DB)
When a store's error rate or queueing latency exceeds the configured threshold, lower-priority token holders are probabilistically denied admission within 200ms on average
End-to-end P99 tail latency for high-priority requests increases by <10% during a regional store incident (measured against baseline)
Canary rollout to 10% of tenant traffic in us-west with telemetry showing correct token accounting and no token leaks for 48 hours
Automated runbook actions created: emergency-enable-full-shed, partial-shed, and graceful-warmup. Links added to incident playbook.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight token-banking service co-located with the routing layer. Tokens represent ephemeral permission to allocate a connection or enqueue a high-cost operation against a downstream store. Tokens are issued per (region, store, tenant, priority) bucket. Admission uses a fast in-process cache + eventual consistent counters served by the coinbank (gRPC) with per-bucket leases. On store degradation signals (latency/error thresholds, queue depth), the coinbank reduces token refill rates for non-mission-critical priorities and engages a probabilistic deny policy based on configured burn-down curves.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (PoC): local token cache + central refill controller; integrate with connection pool admission hook (conn-manager) for redis and DB clients
Phase 2: add multi-region token federation to allow tokens to be borrowed across nearby regions during partial failover (bounded borrow limits)
Phase 3: add tenant-level billing and observability mappings; expose token consumption per-route in Console
Instrument: token_granted, token_denied, token_refill_rate, token_loan, token_reclaim metrics with tenant and priority tags
Safety: tokens should auto-expire (TTL) and token grants should be idempotent for retries to avoid leaks
Trade-offs: eventual consistency of counters may briefly allow transient overcommit; mitigate by conservative refill rates and short TTLs
Fallbacks: if coinbank is unreachable, conn-manager falls back to local heuristics (fixed low watermark) and emits warning metrics
